requirement: For an enabled Habeas plugin, a supported agent session started within a Cargo and mdBook project whose manifest lists `habeas` under `[dev-dependencies]`, as {cite}`requirements.cli.setup` adds it, MUST receive nonblocking agent context from the `SessionStart` hook of {cite}`requirements.integration.symposium_setup_hook`. That context MUST contain exactly one sentence that points to the skill. The sentence says the project uses Habeas and tells the agent to load the `habeas` skill of {cite}`requirements.cli.overview_skill` before starting any work in the project.
rationale:
structural: I found no structural obligation in `requirements.integration.symposium_skill_hook` that needs implementation evidence. Every clause specifies observable behavior:

- **Context delivery.** The text says a session in a Habeas project "MUST receive nonblocking agent context from the `SessionStart` hook". An agent sees the same context whether one hook entry or several produce it, so the number and layout of hook entries is discretionary. The text names no library, type, signature or interface.
- **Hook registration.** That the hook is a Symposium `SessionStart` hook is the structural obligation of the cited `requirements.integration.symposium_setup_hook`. `Cargo.toml#table[package.metadata.symposium.hooks]/pair[event]` already carries the {impl} marker for that requirement. This requirement only cites it, so it adds no registration obligation of its own.
- **Sentence content.** "Exactly one sentence" that says the project uses Habeas and tells the agent to load the `habeas` skill before any work describes output. A different constant or a different way of building the string would still meet the text.
- **Skill reference.** The `habeas` skill belongs to `requirements.cli.overview_skill`, and `requirements.cli.setup` is cited only to identify the dev-dependency. Neither adds a build obligation here.

The code that produces the output is `src/hook.rs#fn[session_start_response]`, which uses `src/hook.rs#const[SKILL_SENTENCE]`. It returns the sentence only for projects that depend on `habeas`. It returns an empty `SessionStart` object otherwise. Finding this code does not turn the required output into a structural obligation. No review roots were supplied, and none are needed. I leave test adequacy to the behavioral criterion.

behavioral: The reviewed tests cover each behavioral obligation of `requirements.integration.symposium_skill_hook`.

**Delivery of nonblocking context from the `SessionStart` hook in an applicable project.**
- `tests/setup.rs#fn[session_start_points_to_the_habeas_skill_once_setup_is_complete]` runs `habeas setup`, then calls `session_start` from both the project root and a nested directory.
- `session_start` runs the `habeas hook session-start` binary. It requires a successful exit and parses the JSON output.
- The test asserts the whole response equals `{"SessionStart":{"additionalContext":<sentence>}}`. That output has no blocking fields.
- `tests/setup.rs#fn[session_start_puts_the_skill_sentence_before_the_setup_advisory]` covers a project that lists `habeas` under `[dev-dependencies]` but is not fully set up. The response has a single `additionalContext` entry.

**Context contains exactly one sentence pointing to the skill.**
- In the configured case, the context equals `SKILL_SENTENCE` exactly. The sentence says the project tracks requirements with Habeas and tells the agent to load the `habeas` skill before starting any work.
- In the incomplete case, the context must start with that sentence. The test also counts occurrences of "`habeas` skill" and asserts the count is exactly 1.

**Real Symposium dispatch.**
- `tests/symposium_hook_smoke.py#def[main]` runs through Symposium itself. It asserts the skill sentence is delivered both before and after setup, and that after setup the context is only the skill sentence.

**Applicability boundaries.**
- `tests/setup.rs#fn[session_start_advises_only_when_setup_is_incomplete]` and `tests/setup.rs#fn[session_start_gives_no_context_outside_habeas_projects]` cover the non-applicable cases. These are a project outside Cargo, a project without Habeas, and `habeas` under `[dependencies]` or `[build-dependencies]`. Each returns no context.
- Those two tests carry markers for the sibling requirements, not the subject. The boundary behavior is stated by the requirement's "whose manifest lists `habeas` under `[dev-dependencies]`" clause, so the subject's own tests rest on the positive cases above. I count no marking gap.

The requirement only cites the setup advisory and the skill description, so those need no further tests here. I found no unresolved ambiguity or untested obligation.

text: For an enabled Habeas plugin, a supported agent session started within a Cargo and mdBook project whose manifest lists `habeas` under `[dev-dependencies]`, as {cite}`requirements.cli.setup` adds it, MUST receive nonblocking agent context from the `SessionStart` hook of {cite}`requirements.integration.symposium_setup_hook`. That context MUST contain exactly one sentence that points to the skill. The sentence says the project uses Habeas and tells the agent to load the `habeas` skill of {cite}`requirements.cli.overview_skill` before starting any work in the project.

Running `habeas setup` in an existing Cargo and mdBook project MUST add Habeas as a dev dependency, configure `habeas mdbook` as its preprocessor, add the badge stylesheet, enable sidebar folding with `output.html.fold.enable` unless the book already sets it, and create `tests/habeas.rs` that calls `habeas::validate()`. Repeating setup MUST avoid duplicate configuration and preserve customized tests and stylesheets. Setup MUST NOT install or modify agent skills.

For an enabled Habeas plugin, a supported agent session started within a Cargo and mdBook project whose manifest lists `habeas` under `[dev-dependencies]`, as {cite}`requirements.cli.setup` adds it, MUST receive a Symposium `SessionStart` hook. The hook MUST check whether the configuration and files required by `requirements.cli.setup`, {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.setup`, and {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.setup.configuration` are present and compatible. If not, it MUST provide nonblocking agent context saying that Habeas Codicem is not fully configured and suggesting `habeas setup`. If setup is complete or no applicable project is found, it MUST provide no setup advisory. The hook MUST NOT modify project files or run setup itself.

Habeas MUST bundle a `habeas` skill whose description tells agents to use it at the start of any work in a Habeas project, naming as signs of one a `habeas` dev-dependency, a `habeas.toml`, `{req}` directives in the book, and `{impl}`, `{test}`, or `{cite}` references in code.

In a project where `habeas setup` has completed, the whole session-start agent context is one sentence such as "This project tracks requirements with Habeas; load the `habeas` skill before starting any work." {test}`requirements.integration.symposium_skill_hook`
